claims.objects: An abstract ordinary Hodge-atom ledger: a type of varieties with a dimension, a rationality predicate, the product with a projective line, and the multiplicity with which an atom occurs in the atomic composition of a variety; together with the residue discriminant and the parity ranks of an atom, and the explicit rational residue matrices of the cubic zero packet and of a curve of genus at least two.
claims.hypotheses: The projective-bundle formula doubles every atomic multiplicity on the product with a projective line; the ordinary non-rationality criterion excludes rationality of a variety carrying an atom that occurs on no variety of dimension at most two below it; on a variety of dimension at most two every occurring atom either already occurs in dimension at most one or has even rank at least three; an atom of even rank two and odd rank at least four occurring in dimension at most one has vanishing residue discriminant; and the cubic carrier has dimension three and carries an atom of even rank two, odd rank ten, and residue discriminant equal to that of the displayed cubic residue matrix.
claims.conclusion: Lean evaluates the residue discriminant of the cubic zero-packet residue as four ninths and of every curve residue as zero, derives from that separation and the parity ranks that the cubic atom occurs on no variety of dimension at most two, and concludes that the product of the cubic threefold with a projective line is not rational.
claims.cautions: The geometric signature and every ordinary Hodge-atom input remain typed premises rather than foundational constructions: Lean does not construct varieties, the A-model F-bundle, the spectral cover, atoms or atomic compositions, the elementary modification, or the residue of a geometric connection, and does not prove that either displayed matrix is that residue. The surface and curve analysis of the manuscript, which uses the point-blowup and projective-bundle formulas, the nef-canonical lemma, and the classification of minimal smooth projective surfaces, enters as the two exclusion premises.

claims.objects: An abstract geometric signature naming smooth complex cubic threefolds, product with projective one-space, projective four-space, and rationality, together with a natural-valued framed primitive-sixth multiplicity; and, for the third terminal, the product-formula signature carrying a distinguished point, the projective spaces, and the product of a variety with a projective space.

The third terminal assumes instead the product formula for a product with a projective space, involutivity of the framed monodromy of a point, and the passage from the exponents of the reduced rank-two block to framed formal monodromy, and derives from them the multiplicity two of the cubic, its doubling under multiplication by a projective line, and the vanishing on projective four-space. claims.conclusion: The named product of the specified cubic carrier with projective one-space is not rational.
claims.cautions: This is the framed-monodromy route, conditional in the manuscript on the reconstruction-tail hypothesis and on the divisor-tagging hypothesis only for surface centers that are neither minimal nor geometrically ruled and, in Lean, on every quantum, weak-factorization, and rational-comparison fact as a typed premise. It is independent of the unconditional atomic route recorded under thm:every-cubic and is not a formalization of that route. The third terminal removes three numerical assumptions in favour of the product formula and the exponent-to-monodromy passage; neither of those is formalized.

claims.objects: The six-point permutation module of the alternating group on five letters over the prime fields of characteristic two and three, its augmentation quotient by the all-ones vector presented in four explicit coordinates, and the matrix commutant of the generated action on that quotient.

claims.conclusion: In each characteristic the four-coordinate chart identifies the heart with the augmentation quotient and carries the two label permutations to the displayed generator matrices; every subspace stable under the generated action is zero or the whole heart, so the heart is simple; the commutant of the generated action is `{0, 1, W, W + 1}` in characteristic two, with `W ^ 2 + W + 1 = 0`, `W (W + 1) = 1` and the four elements pairwise distinct, hence the field with four elements, and consists of the scalar matrices alone in characteristic three, hence the field with three elements.

The endomorphism algebras are exhibited by explicit generators and relations rather than by an isomorphism with named field objects. The manuscript indexes the module by the six conjugate order-ten dihedral subgroups of the alternating group, equivalently the six Sylow-five subgroups with their normalizers, which is a group-theoretic object this package does realize: it constructs the six order-five subgroups, proves that the two generators conjugate them by exactly the displayed label permutations, and computes each normalizer's order as ten. claims.objects: An opaque organizational signature with a base type and dependent fibre types named for the relative elliptic scheme, augmentation-lattice source, intermediate Jacobian, two-primary discriminant, H2 tensor two-torsion model, and isogeny kernel; a fibrewise function, discriminant equivalences, kernel inclusions, the explicit integral matrix 6I5-J5, an independently defined tensor-extended coefficient kernel over an arbitrary F2-module, standard rank-eight discriminant coordinates after choosing a symplectic basis, an explicit linear equivalence of those coordinates with two copies of the six-point coefficient heart, and the rational augmentation representation of the concrete six-point alternating-group action together with each labelled point stabilizer, its fixed subspace, and the linear group norm obtained by summing its ten coordinate-permutation operators. The three-primary branch additionally defines the four-coordinate model of H3 = Aug(F3^6)/<1>, its normalized symmetric coefficient form, the induced alternating form on two heart copies, and the vertical/scalar-graph packet. The transport terminal additionally considers an arbitrary type carrying an action of the concrete alternating group and an object fixed by one labelled stabilizer. claims.hypotheses: Opaque propositions are supplied for every conclusion of the relative lemma: connected smooth-locus and elliptic-scheme status, augmentation-tensor source, isogeny and finite-flatness, A5-equivariance, natural S6-actions, the quotient form induced by 6I6-J6, polarization pullback, five-axis Gram identification, identification of the discriminant with the source-polarization kernel and of the tensor model with H2 tensor E[2], A5-equivariant symplectic discriminant equivalence, identification of the named kernel type with the two-primary kernel of the relative map, injectivity of its discriminant inclusion, and A5-stability and maximal isotropy of that kernel. The kernel-coordinate terminal additionally supplies an equivalence from each named discriminant fibre to the explicit rank-eight coordinates, a subspace whose vectors are exactly the coordinate images of the geometric kernel inclusion, and proofs that this subspace is diagonally stable and maximal isotropic. The three-primary coefficient terminal has no geometric premise: it works over the explicit field F3 with the displayed translation and inversion matrices.
claims.conclusion: The supplied opaque geometric packet is packaged with a kernel-checked integral Smith witness for the five-axis Gram matrix, including explicit two-sided inverse row and column matrices and diagonal diag(1,6,6,6,6). Independently, for every F2-module T, Lean proves that the kernel of the tensor-extended five-axis Gram map is explicitly linearly equivalent to four copies of T. For a two-dimensional tensor factor it has 2^8 elements, and for scalar coefficients its coordinates agree with the normalized six-point coefficient heart Aug(F2^6)/<1>. The normalized dot product on that heart is proved bilinear, alternating, nondegenerate, and invariant under every word in the generated six-point action. After choosing a symplectic basis of the two-dimensional factor, the induced rank-eight tensor-product form is also proved alternating and nondegenerate, and every isotropic four-dimensional subspace is maximal isotropic. The explicit linear equivalence with two heart copies preserves this form and identifies the five projective-line packet members exactly with the diagonally stable maximal-isotropic subspaces of the rank-eight discriminant. In characteristic three, Lean constructs H3 as Aug(F3^6)/<1> and identifies it with four normalized augmentation coordinates. The quotient chart intertwines the induced translation and inversion actions with their displayed matrices and is an isometry for the minus-dot-product form descended through the constant line. The normalized symmetric form is nondegenerate and generator-invariant; the induced rank-eight tensor form is alternating, nondegenerate, and invariant under the diagonal generator actions. Exactly four four-dimensional subspaces are diagonally stable: the vertical half and three scalar graphs; all four are maximal isotropic. From the additional fibrewise kernel-coordinate input, Lean constructs an equivalence from every geometric kernel carrier to its displayed coordinate subspace and proves that every such transported kernel belongs to the five-member packet. Each labelled axis stabilizer in the concrete six-point action has ten elements and is the corresponding dihedral normalizer; its fixed subspace in the rational augmentation representation is exactly the line generated by the vector with coordinate 5 at that label and -1 elsewhere, and therefore has dimension one. The sum N of the ten stabilizer action operators has exactly that line as its range, satisfies N^2=10N, and after scaling by 1/10 is an idempotent projector onto the axis line. Every labelled axis stabilizer is self-normalizing. For any alternating-group action, if an object is fixed by the source stabilizer, then any two group elements carrying the source label to the same target carry that object to the same image. The six rational axis vectors sum to zero; their synthesis map has kernel exactly the constant line, is onto the augmentation representation, induces a linear equivalence from the six-coordinate quotient by the constant line, and intertwines the concrete alternating-group actions. Integrally, subtracting the sixth coordinate gives a linear equivalence from Z^6/Z1 to Z^5; the symmetric 6I6-J6 form descends through the constant line, and in this chart its Gram matrix is exactly 6I5-J5. Every permutation of the six labels induces a quotient map satisfying the identity and multiplication laws, and the descended form is invariant under all these maps.
claims.cautions: Coverage is fragmentary, not a conditional proof of the manuscript lemma: the theorem repackages opaque supplied geometric propositions while independently proving the arithmetic Smith witness and the coefficient-module parts of both primary discriminant calculations. The supplied packet is inert for that independent content: the Smith witness, the tensor-kernel equivalence, the form properties, and the packet classifications are unconditional statements about explicit objects, and the geometric input reappears in the conclusion only as the assertion that it exists. Lean does not identify the explicit three-primary heart and tensor form with the geometric discriminant D3 = H3 tensor E[3], construct E[3] or its Weil pairing, or prove that the actual geometric three-primary kernel is one of the four formal maximal-isotropic halves. The named geometric types, functions, and propositions do not define schemes, relative morphisms, geometric group actions, Weil pairings, polarization kernels, geometric tensor products, or maximal isotropy of the actual geometric kernel. The explicit tensor-kernel and stable-packet equivalences do not construct E[2], a torsion local system, its symplectic pairing, or the geometric classifying map into that packet. The kernel-coordinate bridge assumes rather than constructs the coordinate equivalence, exact kernel image, stability, and maximal isotropy needed to apply the five-member classification. The rational norm theorem concerns only the explicit coordinate representation; it does not construct or identify the manuscript's geometric norm endomorphism or identify its image with an elliptic subvariety of the relative intermediate Jacobian. The transporter theorem proves the abstract group-action coherence implication but does not construct the elliptic schemes, prove that the stabilizer acts trivially on their images, or identify their geometric transport maps. The coefficient-descent theorem proves only the rational representation-theoretic quotient and equivariance; it does not construct the six primitive elliptic-scheme inclusions, prove that their geometric sum is zero, or descend an actual homomorphism of abelian schemes. The integral quotient theorem constructs only the coefficient lattice and descended bilinear form; it does not identify them with an elliptic-power abelian scheme or geometric polarization. Lean does not formalize the remaining proof ingredients, including elliptic images, geometric coherent identifications, primitivity, generic-to-relative transport, abelian-scheme homomorphism rigidity, relative isogenies, finite flatness, Weil and commutator pairings, or the order and maximal-isotropy argument for the actual isogeny kernel.

claims.objects: Lean represents projective lines over concrete fields F4, F5, and F3 as actual Mathlib projectivizations, using the vertical point plus scalar graph points as an affine chart; the concrete F2-bilinear trace-determinant form on F4^2; its induced alternating form on two multiplicity copies; arbitrary abstract coefficient pairings and slopes; the canonical Frobenius field automorphism of F4 and its actions both on affine-chart coordinates and directly on the actual projective line; the transported marked quadratic root and its conjugate; the determinant kernel defining the concrete group SL2(F4); its faithful action on the five points of the natural projective line; the ordinary alternating group on five labelled letters; continuous classifying maps from connected topological bases into finite discrete packets; and a concrete four-coordinate model for the characteristic-two augmentation hyperplane on six points modulo its constant line, with matrices induced by two explicit six-point permutations, an explicit one-factorization of the fifteen pairs of labels, all six Sylow-five subgroups of the concrete alternating group, their normalizers, and explicit dihedral models for those normalizers. The six labels are also mapped explicitly to P1(F5), with translation and inversion induced by two displayed determinant-one matrices, the faithful natural PSL2(F5) action, and the conjugation action of A5 on its six Sylow-five subgroups. The stable-half terminals additionally consider four-dimensional subspaces of two copies of the concrete coefficient heart under the diagonal action of the two displayed generators, the actual projective line P1(F4) with its marked vertical-plus-affine chart, and the explicit alternating polarization form induced on the two heart copies.
claims.hypotheses: The projective classification uses only finiteness and the field axioms. The concrete F4 trace-determinant, maximal-isotropic, and group-order calculations have no added mathematical hypothesis. Matching the human proof, the public trace-rigidity implication takes a supplied unit d in F4 and assumes that multiplication by d preserves the trace against every test element. The more general polarization theorem assumes exactly that a supplied slope is self-adjoint for a supplied pairing; finite-dimensionality is used for its half-dimension statement. The generic persistence terminal assumes a connected base, a finite packet with the discrete topology, a continuous classifying map, and membership of one chosen fibre in a distinguished packet subset. One marked-F4 specialization takes a continuous classifier into the discrete affine chart Option F4; a stronger specialization takes a continuous classifier directly into Projectivization F4 (F4 x F4). These assume that one chosen fibre is one of the two scalar graphs defined by the transported marked root and its root+1 conjugate. The strongest persistence terminal replaces that marked-pair premise by the weaker premise that the chosen projective point is not fixed by coefficientwise Frobenius. The concrete stable-half terminal universally quantifies a subspace of two heart copies and characterizes the exact condition that it have F2-dimension four and be stable under the diagonal translation and inversion actions. The stronger polarization terminal requires no additional premise: it characterizes packet membership by diagonal stability and maximal isotropy. The explicit projective-line equivalence and its five marked chart values require no additional hypothesis.
claims.conclusion: Every projective-line point is uniquely vertical or a scalar graph; P1(F4) has five members and P1(F3) has four. The printed trace-determinant coefficient form and induced two-copy form are nondegenerate, every F4 scalar is self-adjoint, and every scalar graph equals its orthogonal complement, hence is maximal isotropic. Squaring on F4 is identified with the canonical Frobenius field automorphism; it fixes exactly 0 and 1, is involutive, and exchanges every other scalar with a distinct conjugate. On the affine projective chart it acts coefficientwise, fixes exactly the vertical point and graphs of 0 and 1, and its nonfixed locus is exactly the transported marked quadratic root together with root+1. Transporting that action through the proved affine-chart equivalence gives an involution directly on Projectivization F4 (F4 x F4), whose nonfixed locus is exactly the two scalar graph points of the marked root and root+1. The full five-letter symmetric group has order 120; its alternating subgroup has index two and full normalizer. Transported to this labelling, projective Frobenius is a transposition in the nontrivial coset, hence odd; its conjugation preserves both the alternating subgroup and the concrete PSL2(F4) projective image. A determinant unit whose multiplication preserves the trace against every test element is one. The concrete groups SL2(F4) and the alternating group on five letters both have order 60, the center of SL2(F4) is trivial, its faithful five-point projective image consists exactly of the even permutations, and the resulting construction gives an explicit abstract isomorphism SL2(F4) ≃ A5. Every continuous finite-discrete-packet classifying map on a connected base is constant, so membership in any distinguished subset at one fibre persists at every fibre. In particular, this is proved both for a continuous affine-chart F4 classifier and directly for a continuous classifier into the actual projective line when one chosen fibre lies in the marked two-point scalar-graph pair. More strongly, nonfixity under projective Frobenius at one fibre alone identifies that fibre with the marked pair and propagates the exact classification throughout the connected base. For the explicit six-point characteristic-two heart model, normalized representatives recover all four quotient coordinates, the coordinate kernel on the augmentation hyperplane is exactly the constant line, and translation and inversion induce the displayed matrices. The six labels are explicitly equivalent to the actual P1(F5); under this equivalence the two permutations are the projectivizations of (x,y) maps to (x,x+y) and (x,y) maps to (y,-x). These permutations preserve an explicit five-factor one-factorization; the induced factor words exhaust the alternating group on five letters and have exactly the same word kernel as the six-point words, so the generated six-point action is faithfully identified with a concrete A5. Lean constructs all six Sylow-five subgroups in this concrete A5 and proves that conjugation by the two generators acts on them by exactly the original six-point translation and inversion. The explicit P1(F5) labelling is therefore equivalent to the six-member Sylow-five packet. The faithful natural PSL2(F5) action has order 60; the two displayed permutations arise from explicit determinant-one matrices, and Lean constructs an isomorphism PSL2(F5) ≃ A5 that intertwines the full natural projective action with conjugation on the six Sylow-five subgroups. Both of these six-point actions are two-transitive. Every natural PSL2(F5) point stabilizer is proved to be the corresponding ten-element dihedral normalizer and is explicitly equivalent to D5. The six-label equivalence with the Sylow packet intertwines both generators with conjugation, and each point stabilizer is the corresponding normalizer. Each Sylow normalizer has ten elements and is explicitly equivalent to the dihedral group D5. Every subspace stable under both induced heart matrices is zero or the whole heart. A matrix commutes with every word matrix in the full generated heart action exactly when it is one of {0,1,W,W+1}, where W^2+W+1=0. A subspace of two heart copies is four-dimensional and stable under the diagonal generated action exactly when it is the vertical half or the graph of one of the four displayed commutant endomorphisms 0, 1, W, and W+1; the displayed packet has exactly five distinct members. An explicit equivalence with the actual P1(F4) sends the vertical chart point to the vertical half and the affine labels 0, 1, the transported marked root, and root+1 to the corresponding graphs of 0, 1, W, and W+1. The explicit alternating polarization form on the two heart copies is nondegenerate, and these five packet members are exactly the diagonally stable maximal-isotropic subspaces. The chosen linear equivalence from the standard rank-eight tensor discriminant coordinates to two heart copies preserves the bilinear form and transports this exact stable maximal-isotropic packet classification.
claims.cautions: Lean does not identify the six explicit Sylow-five subgroups and their dihedral normalizers with the manuscript's six geometrically named D5 normalizers. It therefore does not identify the proved concrete A5 permutation action, the resulting four-dimensional module, or its quadratic commutant with the manuscript's geometric A5 action, coefficient heart, and F4 commutant. It also does not prove that all geometrically A5-stable simple halves arise from the projective points, identify the geometric permutation stabilizer with the formalized SL2(F4), identify the manuscript's named A5 action with either formalized alternating-group model, prove that named subgroup lies in the stabilizer, classify the geometric S6 and A5 stabilizers, identify the manuscript's geometric odd normalizer element with the formalized Frobenius permutation, or construct the geometric local system, finite principal-kernel packet, or continuous classifying map needed to apply the connected-family persistence theorem. Thus the abstract generated-group, Sylow-five packet, dihedral normalizers, and six-point action identifications, six-point quotient coordinates and quadratic matrix commutant, finite-field enumeration, concrete polarization and maximal-isotropic algebra, determinant trace-rigidity, abstract exceptional-group identification, abstract Frobenius normalizer calculation, and exact connectedness deduction are checked, but the remaining geometric identifications remain absent. The arithmetic that selects the exotic pair is now covered: Lean computes the order of the symmetric group on six letters as 720 and proves that no group of smaller order, and no group of order 9720, admits an injective homomorphism from it, so none of the classified faithful automorphism groups of a smooth cubic threefold contains a copy of it. The classification supplying those orders remains an explicit hypothesis, and Lean does not construct cubic threefolds, their automorphism groups, or the descent of a stable kernel to an automorphism of the intermediate Jacobian.

claims.objects: Lean represents the two-by-two graph-coordinate block matrices over an arbitrary possibly noncommutative ring; actual rectangular coefficient and slope-error matrices of arbitrary finite block ranks over a commutative ring; a dependent family of finite blocks; the literal flattened square matrix on the disjoint union of all block bases; separately indexed base and split coordinates joined by a supplied invertible basis over a coefficient-extension ring; entrywise uniformizer-power divisibility; and the arithmetic cross-depth obtained by intersecting three divisibility conditions with an extended slope-difference valuation.
claims.hypotheses: The graph-coordinate block identity is purely ring-theoretic. The rectangular positive-positive depth theorem uses finite block index types, a Mathlib discrete valuation domain, a chosen irreducible uniformizer, scalar slope parts, and arbitrary integral error matrices. The unit-positive theorem needs only a commutative ring, finite block indices, arbitrary integral slope matrices, and the positive-depth entrywise coefficient condition. The scalar lift-independence theorem uses the same DVR data.
claims.conclusion: The dual-form adjoint convention is equivalent to the coefficient-form convention for an invertible block. The displayed graph-coordinate product has exactly the manuscript's three nonzero blocks, and entrywise membership is equivalent to membership of those blocks. The actual rectangular commutator is A_ij T_j^t - T_i A_ij: the right slope error is transposed. The positive-positive and unit-positive calculations are assembled over a dependent family of finite blocks. Flattening to the disjoint union of block bases gives a literal symmetric weighted matrix lattice whose membership is exactly block symmetry plus all three graph-descent conditions, including diagonal entries and distinct entries within one block. After entrywise scalar extension and a supplied invertible basis change from distinct base coordinates to the flattened split axis, the transported matrix belongs to the weighted lattice exactly when its restricted blocks are symmetric and satisfy those graph-descent conditions. Positive-depth blocks use scalar plus depth-divisible error; at depth zero the error is unrestricted, so no finite-etale or scalar splitting is imposed. Of the cross depth itself Lean proves that divisibility by its uniformizer power is exactly the conjunction of the three power-divisibility conditions, that the sum of the two diagonal depths is at most twice it, which is the midpoint bound of the statement, and that pairing depth zero with a positive-depth block gives exactly that positive depth, which is the unit-block clause. With finite flattened axis, the DVR graph cross-depth formula yields rank-one generation.
claims.cautions: The marked finite-etale graph presentation, existence and orthogonality of the splitting into slope blocks, geometric origin of the coefficient-form adjoint relation, and the assertion that geometric divisor descent is expressed by the supplied graph-coordinate block conditions are not formalized. Lean checks the passage from any supplied splitting-ring basis and graph-descent block data through the transported flattened coefficient lattice and rank-one generation, but not the geometric construction that supplies those data or interprets the conditions as descended divisors. The displayed cross-depth formula is the Lean definition of the depth attached to a pair of blocks, with the slope-difference subtraction truncated and an infinite valuation contributing nothing, so it is not itself a derived identity; what the terminals establish about it is its equivalence with the three divisibility conditions, the midpoint bound, and the unit-block value.

claims.objects: A symmetric matrix-of-ideals submodule on an arbitrary finite index type over a Mathlib discrete valuation ring, with diagonal depths, symmetric cross depths, a chosen irreducible uniformizer, and the span of rank-one matrices internal to that same submodule.
claims.hypotheses: The coefficient ring is a domain and discrete valuation ring, the chosen uniformizer is irreducible, and the cross-depth function is symmetric. The manuscript's completeness and unramifiedness assumptions are stronger than needed and do not enter this algebraic lemma.
claims.conclusion: The weighted lattice equals its internal rank-one span if and only if every distinct pair satisfies twice the cross depth greater than or equal to the sum of the diagonal depths.
claims.cautions: The LinearOrder instance is finite-sum bookkeeping and adds no mathematical restriction. This theorem takes the matrix-of-ideals depth data as input, exactly as the lemma does; construction of those depths from the preceding geometric graph-coefficient lemma is audited separately under lem:graph-coefficient-lattice.

claims.objects: A base coefficient matrix and its entrywise scalar extension; separately indexed finite base and split coordinate systems over the extension ring joined by mutually inverse rectangular matrices; congruence transport into the split weighted matrix-of-ideals lattice; the extended internal rank-one set and span; the canonical elliptic-source exterior algebra over the splitting ring; a target algebra tensor product joined to that source by an injective pullback; the recursively defined squarefree product sum; and the literal degree-k ordinary product submodules before and after scalar extension.
claims.hypotheses: The coefficient extension is faithfully flat and its target is a DVR with the mapped uniformizer irreducible; finite base coordinates, split block-basis types with finite flattened axis, depths, scalar labels, slope-error matrices, and mutually inverse splitting-ring basis matrices are supplied. For the strongest composite, the base coefficient form is symmetric and the restricted blocks of its congruence-transported scalar extension are assumed to satisfy the three actual graph-coordinate descent conditions; Lean derives block symmetry and weighted-lattice membership. The extended realization in the target algebra tensor product maps lattice classes into the scalar extension of the prescribed base divisor submodule and commutes with an injective pullback to the canonical elliptic-source realization. A base class and proposed divided power are supplied, together with exact compatibility identifying their scalar extensions with the realized transported class and every resulting squarefree representative. The origin of the graph-descent conditions and the realization compatibilities are geometric statements in the human proof.
claims.conclusion: Entrywise coefficient extension preserves weighted-lattice membership and internal rank-one matrices in the literal-coordinate special case. More generally, congruence by a supplied invertible splitting-ring basis change preserves scalar rank-one forms, admits explicit inverse recovery, and allows the base and split coordinate types to differ. For the split graph cross-depth lattice, the midpoint criterion and hence extended rank-one generation are discharged internally after that basis change. Every extended lattice member admits a finite rank-one presentation whose squarefree representative is an ordinary product over the splitting ring. Degree-k ordinary product images over the extension lie in the scalar extension of the base degree-k product image. Faithful flatness reflects membership and equality, so base ordinary-product membership of the specified divided power and its factorial power identity descend.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct the manuscript's marked finite-etale splitting extension, its spectral idempotents, or its eigenbasis matrices; the basis-change theorem takes those matrices as supplied data. Lean derives formal weighted-lattice membership from supplied symmetry and graph-descent block conditions, but it does not prove that geometric divisor descent supplies those conditions. It also does not construct the target cohomology realization or actual isogeny pullback and its injectivity, or prove the explicit compatibilities identifying the base cohomology class and its divided power after extension. Base and split axes are distinct, and the supplied S-basis need not descend to R; existence of the splitting and its geometric graph-descent interpretation remain explicit hypotheses. The division-free square-zero expansion behind the manuscript's divided-power identity is proved, as is decomposability and square-zero vanishing of rank-one classes on the canonical elliptic source. What is assumed, for every resulting decomposition, is the compatibility identifying the manuscript's divided power with that squarefree product sum after extension, rather than deriving it geometrically from the divided-power expansion of the proof. The theorem is an exact algebraic splitting-and-descent packet conditional on those geometric inputs, not yet the manuscript's full finite-etale graph theorem. No Chow statement is made.

claims.objects: The explicit five-axis Gram matrix 6I-J, the first coordinate vector, the four displayed complement vectors e_j+(1/5)e_1, their four-dimensional integral unit block 5I-J, the integral Smith diagonal diag(1,6,6,6,6), a four-by-four matrix over F2 consisting of two companion blocks for t^2+t+1, the concrete root-adjoining quadratic F2-algebra, the concrete four-element gluing field F4 and a chosen F2-algebra equivalence between them, the explicit marked-root eigenbasis and repeated-root diagonal form, and a four-by-four scalar matrix over F3. The lifting terminals add the adjointness defect of a matrix for a supplied two-sided inverse of a symmetric Gram matrix, the strictly lower triangular part of a matrix for a chosen linear order on the coordinates, the quotient of the coefficient ring by the ideal generated by p together with the entrywise reduction of matrices along it, and block-diagonal matrices on a disjoint union of coordinate sets. The discriminant terminal adds the integral matrix 6I5-J5 itself, its integral Smith reduction to diag(1,6,6,6,6) with both reduction matrices and their integral inverses, and integral coordinate vectors, multiplication by the matrix being the map to the dual lattice in the same coordinates. The chart terminal adds the chart change of basis, the identity plus the elementary matrix adding the supplied inverse of five times the first coordinate to each other coordinate, its inverse, and the block matrix of the form in that basis.
claims.hypotheses: The orthogonal calculation is over an arbitrary commutative ring with an explicitly supplied inverse of five. The depth calculation and the F2 slope-model calculation use no geometric hypothesis. One spectral-splitting terminal is over an arbitrary commutative ring of characteristic two with a supplied element omega satisfying omega^2+omega+1=0. The concrete splitting terminal instead uses the root-adjoining algebra of the proved irreducible monic polynomial t^2+t+1 over F2 and requires no supplied root or extension. The F3 slope-model terminal is parameterized by an arbitrary scalar value in F3. The lifting terminal is over a commutative domain in which p and 2 are nonzero, with a symmetric Gram matrix carrying a supplied two-sided inverse over the same ring, a linear order on the coordinates, and a residue endomorphism self-adjoint for the entrywise reduction of that inverse; no geometric hypothesis. The orthogonal-summand terminal supplies self-adjointness of each diagonal block and an arbitrary scalar. The discriminant terminal has no hypothesis.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves the first line has norm five, the four complement vectors are orthogonal to it, their Gram matrix is exactly (6/5)(5I-J), det(5I-J)=125 is prime to two and three, and the four non-unit Smith entries have exact depth one at both primes. It also verifies that the displayed F2 slope model has minimal polynomial exactly t^2+t+1, by proving annihilation and irreducibility over F2. Over any supplied characteristic-two commutative ring containing a root omega, Lean identifies the literal same-pattern matrix with the entrywise scalar extension of the F2 matrix, and an explicit invertible basis diagonalizes it as diag(omega,omega+1,omega,omega+1). Lean additionally constructs the concrete root-adjoining extension, proves it finite etale of degree two over F2, constructs a coefficient-algebra equivalence with the concrete F4 used for the gluing packet, proves that the transported marked root lies outside {0,1}, that its Frobenius conjugate is exactly root+1, and that the corresponding two distinct affine-chart points form a projective-Frobenius two-cycle in the five-point gluing packet. It verifies the marked root equation and the same explicit two-sided eigenbasis and diagonalization both in the root-adjoining field and directly over the concrete F4 packet field. The displayed F3 model is literally scalar and commutes with every coefficient matrix. Lean also proves the depth-one lifting step in the generality in which the manuscript states it: every endomorphism of the reduction modulo p that is self-adjoint for the reduced dual coefficient form is the entrywise reduction of a matrix self-adjoint for the dual coefficient form, the witness being the chosen lift corrected by p times the Gram matrix times the strictly lower triangular part of the divided adjointness defect, so that the construction divides by nothing. It proves the two ways that step meets an orthogonal decomposition: a block-diagonal matrix is self-adjoint for a block-diagonal inverse Gram matrix as soon as each block is, so separate lifts assemble and the decomposition is preserved, and a scalar matrix is self-adjoint for every inverse Gram matrix, so a lift extends by a scalar on the complementary summand. Finally, Lean proves that the unimodular summand carries no discriminant: the constant vector lies in the image of 6I5-J5, has value five under the form, the value of the chart's first coordinate line, every integral vector is congruent modulo that image to a combination of the four remaining reduced basis vectors, whose Smith entries have exact depth one at two and at three, and six annihilates the quotient, so at either prime dividing six the primary part is supported on those four coordinates. Over any coefficient ring in which five has an inverse, Lean also proves the decomposition itself as a change of basis: the chart matrix is invertible, its first column is the first coordinate vector and its other columns are the displayed complement vectors, and it carries 6I5-J5 to the block matrix with the unit line of value five and the complementary block (6/5)(5I4-J4). The first chart dual vector is then in the image of the form and every vector is congruent modulo that image to a combination of the four chart dual vectors orthogonal to it.
claims.cautions: The two residue-field matrices are explicit algebraic models only. The concrete finite-etale theorem constructs the quadratic splitting extension of F2 for the displayed companion-block model and transports its marked root to one member of the two-element Frobenius orbit outside {0,1} in F4; the two exotic scalars are not otherwise individually named. It does not construct or identify the manuscript's marked geometric splitting extension. Lean does not prove that the actual six-axis geometric principal kernel or quotient graph has either model as its slope, does not identify the actual three-primary slope with a one-point finite-etale block, and does not prove persistence through the connected smooth component. Thus the geometric assertions about the actual kernels and slopes remain unformalized. The two finite F2 checks use ordinary kernel reduction via decide, with no native-code decision procedure, external certificate, or oracle; all remaining model claims are symbolic kernel-checked proofs. The passage from determinant prime-to-p to the formal Z_p notion of a unimodular lattice is represented arithmetically rather than through a dedicated p-adic lattice structure. The two clauses that previously had neither a terminal nor a fragment are now covered, at the strength of the algebra they state. The lifting terminal is about matrices over a ring: it does not identify the residue endomorphism with the slope of a geometric principal kernel, and the manuscript's separate reduction step at three, surjectivity of Sp_2(Z_3) onto Sp_2(F_3) used to lift a complementary symplectic ruling, is not formalized. The lift itself is the elementary construction that runs in the manuscript's text between statements, so no statement digest covers that text. For the discriminant the manuscript's summand is realized in the chart itself, over any coefficient ring in which five is invertible, which covers the two-adic and three-adic cases it uses; the parallel statement over the integers is recorded through the Smith reduction, whose unimodular coordinate has the constant vector as its reduced basis vector, also of value five, and is a different line from the chart's. Lean does not identify the discriminant group of the coefficient matrix with a geometric isogeny kernel, and the passage from these data to a marked finite-etale graph presentation consumed by the all-degree graph saturation theorem is not formalized.

claims.objects: Lean represents a weighted matrix-of-ideals lattice, its internal rank-one span, a square-zero additive realization in a commutative ring, an abstract integral product subgroup, and explicit natural-number denominator witnesses for the resulting squarefree product representative.
claims.hypotheses: The lattice is exactly rank-one generated; every internal rank-one realization squares to zero; and for every prime p and every relevant finite internal presentation, some multiplier not divisible by p carries its squarefree degree-k product into the integral product subgroup. This is the elementwise denominator condition needed by the manuscript's local-to-global step; finite generation is unnecessary once these witnesses are supplied.
claims.conclusion: A finite internal rank-one presentation exists whose degree-k squarefree product belongs to the integral product subgroup globally and whose factorial multiple equals the kth power of the realized lattice element.
claims.cautions: The six-axis graph divisor lattice, its realization in cohomology, the local charts at two and three, the comparison away from six, production of the denominator witnesses from localization, and identification of divided powers with ordinary divisor products are not formalized here. In particular Lean does not yet prove membership of Theta^4/4! or any geometric divided-power claim, and the special-fibre Neron-Severi caution remains geometric.

claims.objects: A parameter type, a typed family of cubic-threefold objects, a separate type of intermediate-Jacobian objects, the intermediate-Jacobian assignment, predicates for smooth complex cubic status, algebraicity of the primitive minimal class, and universal CH0-triviality.
claims.hypotheses: Every indexed fibre is a smooth complex cubic threefold; the primitive minimal class of every fibre's intermediate Jacobian is algebraic; and for every smooth cubic under consideration Voisin's criterion identifies primitive-minimal-class algebraicity with universal CH0-triviality.
claims.conclusion: Every indexed fibre is universally CH0-trivial.
claims.cautions: Lean proves only the universally quantified logical deduction. The cubic pencil, smooth fibres, intermediate Jacobians, primitive minimal classes, their algebraicity from the six-axis divided-power theorem, Chow groups, universal base change in the CH0 predicate, and Voisin's geometric equivalence are represented by supplied types, functions, predicates, and premises rather than constructed. The argument is fibrewise and asserts neither a horizontal cycle nor a relative decomposition of the diagonal. The deduction itself is one step: Voisin's equivalence is supplied as an iff for every smooth fibre, algebraicity of the primitive minimal class is supplied fibrewise, and the conclusion is their composition. Lean adds no mathematical content beyond checking that the premises compose.

claims.objects: Smooth cubic threefolds in projective four-space, a point of such a threefold, the tangent hyperplane section there, the Hessian matrix of the defining form, the class of forms that split as sums of cubic forms in pairwise disjoint nonempty groups of at most three variables, and the coprime-degree normal form of Yang, Yu and Zhu.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness of the cubic threefold; for the two families, membership in the separated-variable class or in the normal form of that family.
claims.conclusion: The tangent hyperplane section at a point is a cone with that point as vertex if and only if the Hessian of the defining form there has rank at most two, and every smooth cubic threefold in either named class carries such a point.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.  The argument is a coordinate computation together with the projective geometry of cubic threefolds, which is outside the companion's scope.

claims.objects: The coarse-moduli image of the nonstandard invariant cubic pencil of the alternating group on five letters, the Eckardt points of its members, and the coprime-degree family of Yang, Yu and Zhu.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness of the members, the Eckardt criterion of the preceding lemma, and the computed emptiness of the Eckardt scheme of the members listed in the registered evidence bundle.
claims.conclusion: Only finitely many moduli points of the pencil are represented by cubic threefolds carrying an Eckardt point, and in particular only finitely many by cubics projectively equivalent to a member of that family.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.  It rests on the registered evidence bundle, which exhibits Eckardt-free members but does not compute the finite exceptional set.

claims.objects: The intermediate Jacobian of the geometric generic member of the pencil, the six-axis source lattice with the form six times the identity minus the all-ones matrix, its two-primary coefficient heart with commutant the field of four elements, and odd-degree isogenies onto the intermediate Jacobian from products of principally polarized abelian varieties.
claims.hypotheses: The exotic two-primary gluing kernel of the packet proposition, the elliptic factor without complex multiplication at the geometric generic point, odd isogeny degree, and an odd multiple of the product polarization; the last conclusion drops only the polarization condition and keeps the gluing kernel, the non-CM elliptic factor, and odd degree.
claims.conclusion: Such an isogeny has either one factor or two, of dimensions one and four; the second case is realized by every axis, with the one-dimensional factor isogenous to that elliptic factor; and, with no condition imposed on the pulled-back polarization, the intermediate Jacobian receives no odd-degree isogeny from a product of five elliptic curves, even though it is isogenous to the fifth power of that elliptic factor.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.  The statement is about the lattice model established earlier in the same section, and members whose elliptic factor has complex multiplication are excluded by hypothesis.

claims.objects: The coarse-moduli image of the nonstandard invariant cubic pencil of the alternating group on five letters, and cubic forms that split as sums of forms in pairwise disjoint nonempty groups of at most three variables.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness of the pencil members, the separated-variable criterion for universal CH0-triviality of Colliot-Thelene, and the Eckardt criterion together with the registered Eckardt computation inherited through the preceding proposition; the order-three signature route printed after the proof gives the same finiteness without any computation.
claims.conclusion: Only finitely many moduli points of the pencil are represented by cubics projectively equivalent to a separated-variable form, so all but finitely many are universally CH0-trivial for a reason the separated-variable criterion does not supply.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.  The projective-equivalence argument over the coarse moduli image is outside the companion's scope.  Its printed proof runs through the Eckardt criterion and therefore through the registered evidence bundle; the computation-free route is recorded after it.

claims.objects: An endomorphism of a module over a commutative ring and its negative; the kernels of the powers of the endomorphism shifted by a scalar, which are its generalized eigenspaces; the set of its eigenvalues; the submodule generated by the orbit of a vector, whose equality with the whole module is regularity; and the universal discriminant of a monic quartic in its characteristic coefficients.
claims.hypotheses: Only the ring and module structure, and for the discriminant statement that the quartic splits with the four displayed roots.
claims.conclusion: The generalized eigenspace of the negated endomorphism at the negated scalar is the generalized eigenspace of the original one, for every exponent; the eigenvalue set of the negated endomorphism is the image of the original eigenvalue set under negation and has the same cardinality; the submodule generated by the orbit of a vector is the same for both, so the two endomorphisms are regular together; and negating the four roots of a split monic quartic leaves its discriminant unchanged.  The residue discriminant of a two-by-two residue is likewise unchanged by sign reversal, and the universal quartic discriminant is unchanged when the coefficients of the linear and cubic terms are negated, without assuming the quartic splits.
claims.cautions: Fragment. The companion contains no F-bundle, F-manifold, or spectral cover, and does not prove that the residual endomorphism of the A-model connection in the loop coordinate is the negative of Euler multiplication; that reading of the connection is the content of the manuscript's lemma and is assumed. What is proved is the linear algebra and the coefficient identity that the reading is then used for.

claims.objects: A commutative algebra over a commutative ring with a family of algebra automorphisms, the subalgebra of its simultaneous fixed points, multiplication by a fixed element and its restriction to that subalgebra, the span of the first four powers of a fixed element, and the truncated polynomial algebra of exponent four over a field.
claims.hypotheses: That the family acts by algebra automorphisms, that the distinguished element is fixed, and, for the dimension count, that its first four powers are linearly independent.
claims.conclusion: The fixed points form a subalgebra; multiplication by a fixed element preserves it and the restricted product is the product of the subalgebra, so an eigenvector of the restriction is an eigenvector of the ambient multiplication with the same eigenvalue; the powers of a fixed element lie in the fixed subalgebra and four independent powers span a four-dimensional subspace; and the truncated polynomial algebra of exponent four realizes that configuration, with vanishing fourth power and dimension four.
claims.cautions: Fragment. Lean constructs no cohomology, no quantum product, and no F-bundle, and does not prove that the Hodge-fixed locus of the maximal A-model F-bundle is smooth, that its tangent space is the Novikov extension of the rational classes of Hodge type (i, i), or that the Lefschetz theorem identifies that space with the even cohomology of a cubic threefold. Equivariance of the multiplication appears as the hypothesis of an action by algebra automorphisms, and the identification of the resulting algebra with the truncated polynomial algebra is not proved.

claims.objects: The doubled Euler multiplication matrix and the grading matrix of the small even quantum connection of a smooth cubic threefold in the ordered classical basis, written over a characteristic-zero field in a nonzero square root r of three times the line-class Novikov variable; the constant separating change of basis; two explicit block-off-diagonal gauge coefficients; the rank-two zero block with its canonical elementary modification; and, for the gauge statements, the partition of the four coordinates into the two simple Euler eigenvalues and the rank-two zero block, the separated system whose coefficients are the separated Euler matrix and the separated grading matrix, and the notion of a normalized gauge: one starting at the identity whose positive coefficients are block off-diagonal, carrying the system to one whose every coefficient is block diagonal, through the inverse-free coefficientwise identity relating the two systems.
claims.hypotheses: The field has characteristic zero and r is nonzero. No property of the two displayed connection matrices is assumed; they are the matrices exhibited in the source.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves that the separating change of basis has determinant -486 r^5, conjugates the Euler matrix to the diagonal pair 6r, -6r together with a single rank-two Jordan block at zero, and conjugates the grading matrix to the displayed separated form; that the two supplied gauge coefficients make the first and second coefficients of the transformed system block diagonal, with rank-two blocks diag(-19/18, 19/18) and the displayed second block; and that the residue of the canonical elementary modification is the displayed matrix, of trace -1 and determinant 5/36, whose characteristic polynomial is the rank-two indicial polynomial. Lean also proves that the separated system has a normalized gauge and that any two normalized gauges of it agree at every order, the separated Euler matrix being block diagonal for the partition with unit differences of its three eigenvalues and a square-zero difference from their diagonal matrix; and that for every normalized gauge the first two gauge coefficients are the two exhibited matrices and the first two coefficients of the reduced system are the exhibited block-diagonal ones.
claims.cautions: This is a strictly weaker fragment of the manuscript statement. The normalized gauge is now proved to exist and to be unique, and the exhibited coefficients are identified as its first two, but the reduction is carried out only to the second order, which is the order the residue needs; no third or higher coefficient is computed. Lean does not construct the quantum connection and does not prove that the displayed matrices are the small even connection of a cubic threefold; that identification is the imported datum.

claims.objects: The discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of Euler multiplication on a four-dimensional F-manifold, presented as the universal discriminant polynomial in four ring elements playing the role of the characteristic coefficients, four derivations of that ring playing the role of the canonical frame of powers of the Euler field, and, for the vanishing statement, the ring of formal power series over a commutative domain of characteristic zero as a model of the germ at the base point.
claims.hypotheses: The sixteen coefficient identities by which the canonical frame acts on the characteristic coefficients, in the conventions that the leading coefficient is one and coefficients of negative index vanish; for the differential statement, an expression of the operator as a ring-coefficient combination of the frame; for the vanishing statement, such an expression of every formal partial derivative, which is regularity of Euler multiplication at the base point, together with vanishing of the constant coefficient of the discriminant.
claims.conclusion: The unit field annihilates the discriminant, the Euler field multiplies it by twelve, and the second and third powers of the Euler field multiply it by minus six times the cubic coefficient and by six times the square of the cubic coefficient minus ten times the quadratic coefficient; every frame combination therefore multiplies the discriminant by a ring element, which is the statement that the differential of the discriminant is the discriminant times a regular one-form; and a discriminant vanishing at the base point is the zero power series. The universal discriminant polynomial is also identified with the squared product of the pairwise root differences of a split quartic. The frame data is also exhibited in the universal root model, the polynomial ring in four root variables with the s-th frame field acting by the derivation given by the sum of the s-th powers of the variables against the corresponding partial derivatives, so the sixteen coefficient identities are consistent.
claims.cautions: Lean constructs no F-manifold, tangent sheaf, Euler field, or spectral cover, and derives the sixteen coefficient identities from neither Cayley-Hamilton nor the Witt relations of a regular F-manifold: they are hypotheses of the frame data. The germ is modelled by a formal power-series ring; the completion of the local ring of a rigid-analytic germ, its isomorphism with that ring, and the injectivity supplied by Krull's intersection theorem are not formalized.

claims.objects: A finite-dimensional commutative algebra over a field, an element of that algebra, a module over it carrying a compatible base-field structure, and a module vector along which the algebra acts injectively.
claims.hypotheses: The algebra is finite dimensional over the base field, and the map sending an algebra element to its action on the chosen vector is injective.
claims.conclusion: The set of base-field eigenvalues of the element acting on the module equals its set of eigenvalues acting on the algebra.
claims.cautions: Lean constructs no quantum cohomology, F-bundle, Hodge base, or Euler field, and proves neither that even quantum cohomology is finite dimensional over its coefficient field nor that the unit of the cohomology ring generates an injective copy of the even part. The formal proof replaces the manuscript's decomposition into generalized eigenspaces by the fact that a non-unit of a finite-dimensional commutative algebra is a zero divisor, so the idempotent decomposition is neither formalized nor needed.

claims.objects: The truncated Chern class arithmetic of a cubic hypersurface in projective four-space in a commutative ring where the fourth power of the hyperplane class vanishes; the Betti numbers of the threefold as an integer-valued function of the degree; the cohomological degree reached by Euler multiplication from degree three in a given Novikov degree; and a locally constant rank function on a topological space modelling the generalized eigenbundle rank on the spectral cover.
claims.hypotheses: Vanishing of the fourth power of the hyperplane class; the Lefschetz Betti numbers in the even degrees and in degrees one and five; the equality of the alternating sum of the Betti numbers with the top Chern number, whose value comes from the Chern class identity and the degree three of the hyperplane class cubed; even rank two from the block reduction of the small even connection; local constancy of the rank on the cover; and the three fibre ranks twelve, one, and one.
claims.conclusion: The adjunction quotient of the fifth power of one plus the hyperplane class by one plus three times it is one plus two times it plus four times its square minus twice its cube, so the third Chern class is minus twice the cube; the third Betti number is ten; the cohomology vanishes in every degree Euler multiplication reaches from degree three, so the whole degree-three cohomology lies in the zero packet; the branch of rank twelve lies in a connected component containing neither rank-one branch; and the parity ranks of the zero packet are two and ten, of total rank twelve.  The adjunction factor is a unit in the truncated ring, so that Chern class is the unique solution of the adjunction equation rather than one consistent value.
claims.cautions: Fragment. Lean constructs no variety, cohomology, Chern class, quantum product, spectral cover, or Hodge atom. That the small hyperplane point lies in the maximal-eigenvalue locus, that the reduced spectral cover is finite etale there, that the generalized eigenbundles are locally free with locally constant rank, and that a connected component of the cover defines a Hodge atom are geometric inputs and appear only as the hypotheses displayed above.

claims.objects: Square matrices over a commutative ring: a connection matrix with a simple pole in the loop coordinate, presented by its residue and the coefficient family of its regular part; the coefficient family of a sesquilinear pairing whose right argument is evaluated at the negated loop coordinate; and the coefficientwise image of the pairing under the derivation of the chosen direction.
claims.hypotheses: The pairing is constant in the chosen frame: its leading coefficient is a supplied matrix and every higher coefficient vanishes. The residue of the connection is self-adjoint for that matrix, and the regular part is a supplied anti-self-adjoint matrix in degree zero and vanishes in every higher degree. For a base direction, the derivation is assumed to annihilate every pairing coefficient.
claims.conclusion: Every coefficient of the sesquilinear horizontality identity vanishes, both in the loop direction, whose derivation multiplies the coefficient of the loop coordinate to the power of an order by that order, and in every direction whose derivation annihilates the pairing.
claims.cautions: Lean constructs no F-bundle, quantum product, Poincare pairing, or grading operator, and proves neither the Frobenius property of quantum multiplication nor anti-self-adjointness of the grading operator; both enter as hypotheses about matrices. The terminal proves the substitution step of the manuscript proof: granted self-adjointness of the residue and anti-self-adjointness of the regular part in degree zero, the coefficients of the horizontality identity cancel term by term. Both adjointness statements are hypotheses here, and what they stand for is where the mathematical content of the manuscript lemma lies: the Frobenius property of the non-archimedean quantum product together with constancy of the inverse Gram matrix in the standard cohomology frame, neither of which is formalized. No convergence, analytic structure, or cohomological grading is represented.

claims.objects: The leading operators of two local spectral factors, each a scalar plus a nilpotent matrix over a field, the coefficient families of the connections on the two factors and of the pairing between them, the coefficientwise image of that pairing under the derivation of the chosen direction, and block matrices assembled from two diagonal blocks and vanishing off-diagonal blocks; and, for an arbitrary splitting, a finite type of coordinates carrying a factor label and a parity in the integers modulo two, a connection whose residue and regular coefficients vanish on entries with differently labelled row and column, an injective family of leading eigenvalues, and the restriction of a matrix to the coordinates satisfying a predicate.
claims.hypotheses: The two leading eigenvalues are distinct and the remaining parts of both leading operators are nilpotent. For the derived form, every coefficient of the sesquilinear horizontality identity between the two factors vanishes, and the direction's derivation annihilates a vanishing pairing coefficient; for the abstract form, the leading order of horizontality is supplied as a Sylvester equation and each later order as the same equation with a right-hand side that vanishes once all strictly earlier off-diagonal coefficients vanish. For an arbitrary labelled splitting: the leading eigenvalues are pairwise distinct, the residue restricted to the coordinates of one label is that eigenvalue plus a nilpotent matrix, the residue and every regular coefficient are block diagonal for the label, every coefficient of the horizontality identity vanishes, and the derivation annihilates an entry at which the pairing vanishes. For the nondegeneracy statements: the pairing vanishes on entries whose row and column carry different labels and on entries whose row and column carry different parities, and its determinant is nonzero.
claims.conclusion: The Sylvester equation has only the zero solution; horizontality is order by order that equation for one pairing coefficient with a remainder built from strictly earlier coefficients, so every coefficient of the pairing between the two factors vanishes by induction on the order; and a pairing with vanishing off-diagonal blocks is invertible exactly when both diagonal restrictions are. For an arbitrary labelled splitting, the block of the horizontality identity between two labels is the two-factor identity of the corresponding blocks, so every coefficient of the pairing vanishes on every entry whose row and column carry different labels. A nondegenerate pairing that is block diagonal for the labels and pairs only coordinates of equal parity restricts to a nondegenerate pairing on the coordinates of one label, and on the coordinates of one label and even parity; reindexing the latter along any bijection with a finite ordinal preserves nonvanishing of the determinant, which is the invertibility hypothesis of the rank-two residue rigidity argument. Distinctness of the leading eigenvalues cannot be dropped: for any scalar, two one-dimensional factors with that same scalar residue, vanishing regular part, and a constant pairing with invertible leading coefficient satisfy every coefficient of the horizontality identity while the pairing between them is nonzero.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct the F-bundle, the spectral splitting, the connection, the cohomological grading, or the Poincare pairing; the connection is represented by a residue and a regular coefficient family, the pairing by a coefficient family of matrices, the splitting by a label on a finite type of coordinates, and the parity by an arbitrary function to the integers modulo two with zero naming the even coordinates. Block diagonality of the connection in the chosen frame, and the vanishing of the pairing between coordinates of different parity, are hypotheses rather than consequences of a geometric construction; nondegeneracy is nonvanishing of a determinant rather than a property transported from a geometric pairing.

claims.objects: The square-zero part of the centered leading Euler operator of an even rank-two atomic factor, the coefficient family of the horizontal Poincare pairing in a chosen frame, and the coefficient family of the connection in the loop direction, all as two-by-two matrices over a field in which two is invertible, together with the coefficients of the sesquilinear horizontality identity built from them.
claims.hypotheses: The leading operator part squares to zero and is nonzero, and the leading pairing coefficient is invertible. Horizontality enters either as the two displayed matrix equations -- self-adjointness of the leading operator part for the leading pairing coefficient, and the constant coefficient relating the regular coefficient, the two leading pairing coefficients, and the leading operator part -- or, in the derived form, as vanishing of the coefficients of the loop-direction horizontality identity at the order of the inverse loop coordinate and at the constant order.
claims.conclusion: The coefficient of the inverse loop coordinate is exactly self-adjointness of the leading operator part, and the constant coefficient is exactly the four-term relation; from those, the regular coefficient carries the nilpotent line into itself, in the equivalent matrix form that the leading operator part, the regular coefficient, and the leading operator part again have vanishing product, together with its vector form: every vector in the image of the leading operator part is carried into its kernel.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct the A-model F-bundle, the spectral cover, the atomic factor, or the Poincare pairing, and does not prove nondegeneracy of the pairing on a separated spectral factor; those supply the hypotheses. Horizontality of the pairing is represented as vanishing of the coefficients of a formal identity between matrix coefficient families, not as a property of a geometric connection. The line is presented as the image of the leading operator part rather than as a subobject of a geometric bundle.

claims.objects: The connection of a centered rank-two factor as a formal object: the loop and base connection matrices, each with a simple pole, are represented by the power series obtained from them by clearing that pole, so that flatness and horizontality of the sesquilinear pairing are single identities of formal power series with matrix coefficients; the canonical elementary modification, constructed as the gauge diag(1, u) and applied to both directions without inverses or Laurent series; the residue of the modified lattice and its discriminant, the square of the trace minus four times the determinant; a map of the coefficient ring that is additive and satisfies the Leibniz rule, applied entrywise, modelling a base vector field; and, for the germ statement, the ring of multivariate formal power series in the coordinates of the germ over a field of characteristic zero, with its formal partial derivatives as the coordinate directions.
claims.hypotheses: The frame is adapted: the leading coefficient of the loop direction is the square-zero matrix whose only nonzero entry is an invertible upper-right entry, the unit coming from the leading Euler operator. Two is invertible in the coefficient ring, which over the germ ring is automatic. The pairing is horizontal for the loop direction and its leading coefficient has invertible determinant, which is nondegeneracy in the form the germ ring supports; and the pair of connection matrices is flat, in every coordinate direction for the germ statement. The two final terminals instead assume the coefficient equations directly: for the first, that the upper-right entry of the residue is invertible and that the order minus-one coefficient of flatness in the modified lattice vanishes; for the second, that the entrywise derivation carries the residue to its commutator with a supplied regular matrix.
claims.conclusion: Flatness forces the leading coefficient of the modified base direction to vanish, so the modified connection is regular in that direction; the next order of flatness is then the Lax equation, with the regular coefficient of the modified base direction itself as the conjugating matrix rather than a supplied one; consequently every derivation of the coefficient ring annihilates the residue discriminant, and over the germ that discriminant equals the constant series with its own constant coefficient, so it does not vary over the germ. Horizontality of the pairing, not an assumption on the connection, supplies the property of the regular coefficient that the modification needs. The two final terminals record the same vanishing of the residual pole and the same annihilation of the discriminant from the supplied coefficient equations alone.
claims.cautions: The geometry is not constructed and remains the input, exposed as typed premises: that an atomic factor of the A-model F-bundle supplies a connection of this shape in an adapted frame, that the Poincare pairing of that factor is the horizontal pairing of the connection, and that the formal power-series model computes the germ of the spectral component. Lean builds no F-bundle, spectral cover, connected component of one, or geometric lattice, and the centering of the scalar irregular part is part of the presentation rather than a formalized step. Constancy is proved over the formal germ, not analytic local constancy on a rigid chart.

claims.objects: The residue of the canonical modified lattice as a two-by-two matrix over a commutative ring, together with two ring elements presented as its eigenvalues through its trace and determinant.
claims.hypotheses: The trace of the residue is the sum of the two supplied elements and its determinant is their product, which is what splitting the characteristic polynomial supplies.
claims.conclusion: The residue discriminant is the squared separation of the two eigenvalues, and it is unchanged by adding a scalar multiple of the identity to the residue, so it is insensitive to a scalar normalization.
claims.cautions: Only the second assertion of the proposition is formalized. The identification of the eigenvalue classes modulo the integers with the formal exponent classes of the centered rank-two module rests on the formal classification of regular-singular differential modules, which Lean does not construct, and the meromorphic gauge implementing the modification is not represented.

claims.objects: Square matrices over a field on a finite type of coordinates carrying a factor label, a pair of mutually inverse matrices that are block diagonal for that label, the block of a matrix on the coordinates of one label, and a frame presenting an even rank-two factor as a two-by-two matrix; and, for the normalization statements, matrices over a commutative ring split into blocks by a labelling of the coordinates, the Sylvester operator of two leading operators, a system with a second-order pole given by the family of its coefficients, and a gauge acting on it through the inverse-free coefficientwise identity, normalized by starting at the identity with block off-diagonal positive coefficients.
claims.hypotheses: The two matrices of the change of frame are mutually inverse, and both vanish on entries whose row and column carry different labels. For the Sylvester statement, each of the two leading operators is a scalar multiple of the identity plus a nilpotent matrix and the two scalars differ by a unit; for the block and gauge statements, the leading operator is block diagonal, the scalars attached to distinct labels differ by units, and the operator differs from the diagonal matrix of those scalars by a nilpotent matrix.
claims.conclusion: The block of a conjugated matrix on one factor is the conjugate of that factor's block by the corresponding diagonal blocks, which are themselves mutually inverse; consequently the residue discriminant of an even rank-two factor, read through any frame, is unchanged by the change of frame. Separately, the Sylvester equation of two operators with separated spectra has exactly one solution for every right-hand side; every block off-diagonal matrix is the commutator of the leading operator with exactly one block off-diagonal matrix; and a system whose leading coefficient is block diagonal with separated blocks admits a normalized gauge reducing it to block-diagonal form, unique in the sense that two normalized gauges agree at every order and so do the two reduced systems.
claims.cautions: Lean constructs no F-bundle, spectral cover, connected component of one, or local factor, and proves no gluing: the transition data enter as a supplied block-diagonal pair of mutually inverse matrices, and the invariance conclusion is that of one conjugation-invariant expression rather than the existence of a glued factor or the meromorphy of an expression formed from it. The normalization statements are the algebra of the manuscript's uniqueness argument, at the level of formal coefficient families: no connection, analytic gauge, or local analytic splitting is constructed, the existence of the analytic splittings being the imported datum, and nothing is proved about convergence or about the overlaps on which the imported splittings are compared.

claims.objects: A two-by-two matrix over a ring of multivariate formal power series over a characteristic-zero domain, modelling the residue over a formal germ of the base; a family of matrices over the same ring, one for each variable, modelling the regular matrices of the modified flatness equation; and the coefficientwise formal partial derivatives of that ring, whose additivity and Leibniz rule are proved.
claims.hypotheses: Each formal partial derivative of the residue is its commutator with the regular matrix of that variable, which is what modified flatness asserts in each base direction.
claims.conclusion: Every formal partial derivative of the residue discriminant vanishes, and a series all of whose formal partial derivatives vanish has no coefficient outside the constant term, so the residue discriminant is the constant series with its own constant coefficient: it does not vary over the germ.
claims.cautions: The germ is modelled by a formal power-series ring. Lean constructs no analytic or rigid-analytic germ, no spectral cover and no connected component of one, and proves neither the meromorphic extension across the locus where the leading operator degenerates, nor normality, connectedness, or irreducibility of that component, nor the identification of the formal model with a geometric germ. Constancy on a formal germ is therefore weaker than constancy on the manuscript's connected component.

claims.objects: Two-by-two residue matrices over a commutative ring, a pair of mutually inverse matrices acting by conjugation, and the addition of a scalar multiple of the identity.
claims.hypotheses: The two conjugating matrices are mutually inverse.
claims.conclusion: The residue discriminant is unchanged by conjugation, because conjugation preserves the trace and the determinant, and is unchanged by conjugation followed by adding any scalar multiple of the identity.
claims.cautions: This is the first half of the manuscript proof, the invariance under an isomorphism of atomic F-bundles, reduced to its matrix algebra. Lean constructs no ordinary Hodge atom, atomic F-bundle, isomorphism of such, or elementary modification, and does not prove that an isomorphism acts on the residue by conjugation and trace recentering, that the even rank and the generic nonvanishing of the leading operator are preserved, or that the image of the leading operator is carried to the corresponding line. The second half, independence of the base point within a connected component of the spectral cover, is the separate crossing row, and the gluing of local factors over that component is a further separate row with no formal counterpart.

claims.objects: An ordinary Hodge-atom ledger with a dimension and an atomic multiplicity, the parity ranks and residue discriminant of an atom, the genus of a curve, and the explicit rational residue matrix of the cubic zero packet.
claims.hypotheses: The atom has even rank two, odd rank ten, and the residue discriminant of the displayed cubic residue matrix. On a variety of dimension at most one, every occurring atom is supplied to be either of even rank one, the point case, or of parity ranks two and twice the genus with vanishing residue discriminant, the nef-canonical curve case.
claims.conclusion: A variety of dimension at most one carrying the atom would have genus five, and no variety of dimension at most one carries it at all, because the residue discriminant of the cubic atom evaluates to four ninths while a curve atom has vanishing residue discriminant.
